title: Symplectic Manifolds Moser Stability and Darboux Weinstein Theory

items.title: Symplectic vector space
items.statement: A symplectic vector space is a finite-dimensional real vector space with a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form.
items.proof_plan: Define nondegeneracy by the flat-map isomorphism and include dimension zero.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Symplectic vector spaces have even dimension
items.statement: Every symplectic vector space has even dimension and a standard symplectic basis.
items.proof_plan: Apply the alternating normal form; nondegeneracy eliminates its radical.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Symplectic orthogonal complement
items.statement: For W≤V, W^ω consists of vectors pairing to zero with every vector in W.
items.proof_plan: Verify it is the inverse image of the annihilator under ω-flat.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Symplectic double orthogonal and dimension identities
items.statement: For W≤V, dim W+dim W^ω=dim V and (W^ω)^ω=W.
items.proof_plan: Transport finite-dimensional annihilator identities through ω-flat.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Isotropic coisotropic symplectic and lagrangian subspaces
items.statement: Define W as isotropic, coisotropic, symplectic, or Lagrangian by W⊆W^ω, W^ω⊆W, W∩W^ω=0, or W=W^ω respectively.
items.proof_plan: Record all inclusions literally to prevent convention drift.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Equivalent characterizations of lagrangian subspaces
items.statement: In dimension 2n, Lagrangian means equivalently isotropic of dimension n or maximal isotropic.
items.proof_plan: Use the dimension identity and extend an isotropic basis to a symplectic basis.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Symplectic reduction of a coisotropic vector subspace
items.statement: For coisotropic W, ω descends to a symplectic form on W/W^ω.
items.proof_plan: Check representatives and identify the descended radical with zero.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Graphs of linear maps and lagrangian relations
items.statement: The graph of A:V→W is Lagrangian in V^-×W iff A is a symplectic isomorphism.
items.proof_plan: Evaluate the product form on graph vectors and use the half-dimension condition.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Symplectic form and symplectic manifold
items.statement: A symplectic form is a smooth closed two-form that is pointwise nondegenerate.
items.proof_plan: State both closedness and nondegeneracy, including the zero-dimensional boundary case.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Nondegeneracy is equivalent to a nonvanishing top wedge
items.statement: On a 2n-manifold, ω is nondegenerate exactly when ω^n is nowhere zero.
items.proof_plan: Compute the top wedge in a symplectic basis; a radical vector forces vanishing conversely.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Symplectic manifolds have a canonical orientation and volume form
items.statement: The form ω^n/n! canonically orients a symplectic 2n-manifold and is its symplectic volume.
items.proof_plan: Use its nowhere-vanishing positive ray.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Symplectomorphism local symplectomorphism and symplectic embedding
items.statement: Define symplectomorphisms, local symplectomorphisms, and symplectic embeddings by exact pullback equality of forms.
items.proof_plan: Distinguish global bijectivity, local diffeomorphism, and embedding.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Products and opposites of symplectic manifolds
items.statement: Products carry pr_M*ω+pr_N*η and the opposite carries -ω; both are symplectic.
items.proof_plan: Use pullback calculus for closedness and the tangent-space splitting for nondegeneracy.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Isotropic coisotropic symplectic and lagrangian submanifolds
items.statement: Define the four submanifold notions by the corresponding property of every tangent space.
items.proof_plan: Require an embedded constant-dimensional submanifold.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Lagrangian submanifolds have half dimension
items.statement: A Lagrangian submanifold of a 2n-manifold has dimension n.
items.proof_plan: Apply the linear result tangent-spacewise.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Tautological one form on a cotangent bundle
items.statement: On π:T*Q→Q, λ_(q,p)(ξ)=p(dπξ), and the library defines ω_can=-dλ.
items.proof_plan: Give the intrinsic evaluation and fix the sign before coordinates.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: The tautological one form is intrinsic and smooth
items.statement: The tautological formula is intrinsic and smooth, with λ=Σp_i dq^i in cotangent coordinates.
items.proof_plan: Use projection/evaluation intrinsically, then compute local coefficients.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: The canonical cotangent two form is symplectic
items.statement: The form -dλ=Σdq^i∧dp_i is symplectic on T*Q.
items.proof_plan: Use d²=0 and contract a general tangent vector to prove nondegeneracy.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Cotangent lifts are symplectomorphisms
items.statement: Cotangent lifts of diffeomorphisms preserve λ and therefore ω_can.
items.proof_plan: Evaluate λ using the commuting bundle projections, then differentiate.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Graph of a one form is lagrangian iff the one form is closed
items.statement: The graph of α∈Ω¹(Q) is Lagrangian in T*Q iff dα=0.
items.proof_plan: Pull λ and -dλ back by the graph section and use half dimension.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Compatible complex structure on a symplectic vector space
items.statement: A compatible J has J²=-I, preserves ω, and makes g(u,v)=ω(u,Jv) positive definite.
items.proof_plan: State compatibility, not merely tameness.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: Definition 2.24 and the calculation following it, pp. 13--14

items.title: Compatible complex structures exist on symplectic vector spaces
items.statement: Every finite-dimensional symplectic vector space admits a compatible complex structure.
items.proof_plan: For an auxiliary inner product let A represent ω, put P=(-A²)^{1/2}, and J=P^{-1}A; verify all clauses.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Positive definite bundle endomorphisms have smooth positive square roots
items.statement: A smooth positive-definite self-adjoint bundle endomorphism has a unique smooth positive square root.
items.proof_plan: Use local spectral functional calculus on compact spectral intervals; uniqueness glues the local roots.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: Theorem 2.26 and its fibrewise use before Definition 3.31, pp. 14 and 42

items.title: Every symplectic manifold admits a compatible almost complex structure
items.statement: Assuming AC_ω, every symplectic manifold admits a smooth compatible almost-complex structure.
items.proof_plan: Use the AC_ω-supplied metric and the bundlewise polar construction. This is the exact choice use.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: Discussion preceding Definition 3.31, p. 42, using Theorem 2.26

items.title: Compatible almost kahler metric
items.statement: For compatible J, g(u,v)=ω(u,Jv) defines the associated almost Kähler metric.
items.proof_plan: Verify symmetry and positivity from compatibility.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Compatible almost complex structures and kahler geometry
items.statement: An almost Kähler structure is Kähler only when J is integrable; compatibility alone does not imply this.
items.proof_plan: Separate algebraic compatibility from differential integrability.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Moser pullback differentiation equation
items.statement: For generator X_t, d/dt(φ_t*ω_t)=φ_t*(dotω_t+L_Xtω_t); when dotω_t=dσ_t, solve ι_Xtω_t=-σ_t.
items.proof_plan: Apply the pullback formula and Cartan, keeping the contraction sign.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Smooth parametric primitives for a smooth exact family on a compact manifold
items.statement: A smooth exact family α_t on compact M has jointly smooth primitives β_t; once the compact manifold and family are supplied, this construction itself uses only finite choices.
items.proof_plan: Extract a finite coordinate-ball cover, use the compact-set bump lemma to make its finite shrinking and partition explicitly, and use fixed local homotopy operators with finite Mayer–Vietoris corrections. These give one fixed linear right inverse on exact forms, hence preserve parameter smoothness; only finitely many witnesses are selected.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Moser stability theorem
items.statement: Assuming AC_ω, on compact M a smooth closed-interval path of cohomologous symplectic forms is carried to ω_0 by an isotopy from the identity; smooth on [0,1] means locally smoothly extendible in time at endpoints.
items.proof_plan: Use the fixed finite primitive construction on the closed interval; flatten time by the standard smooth step so the rescaled Moser field extends by zero to an open interval, invoke smooth evolution and compactness, then recover smooth original-time isotopy from the integral equation.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Compact support moser stability on a noncompact manifold
items.statement: If dotω_t=dσ_t with all σ_t supported in one compact set, Moser stability holds on a noncompact manifold by a compactly supported isotopy.
items.proof_plan: Solve the contraction equation, retain common compact support, invoke the global compact-support evolution theorem, and differentiate.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Relative poincare primitive near a submanifold
items.statement: Assuming AC_ω, a closed form vanishing on an embedded S has, near S, a primitive that also vanishes on S, smoothly in parameters.
items.proof_plan: Contract a tubular neighborhood fibrewise and apply the homotopy operator; the endpoint pullback is zero. AC_ω is exactly inherited from the tube.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Relative moser theorem
items.statement: Forms agreeing along S and joined by a locally symplectic interpolation are locally symplectomorphic by a map fixed on S.
items.proof_plan: Use the relative primitive, solve Moser's equation with X_t|S=0, and shrink to a common flow neighborhood.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Darboux theorem
items.statement: Every symplectic form is locally Σdq^i∧dp_i.
items.proof_plan: Match its value at a point to the linear normal form, interpolate with the constant form, and apply relative Moser at that point.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Symplectic manifolds have no local invariants beyond dimension
items.statement: Symplectic manifolds of equal dimension are locally symplectomorphic near arbitrary chosen points.
items.proof_plan: Compose their Darboux charts.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Symplectic normal bundle of a symplectic submanifold
items.statement: For symplectic S⊂M, the symplectic normal bundle is (TS)^ω, a symplectic complement of TS.
items.proof_plan: Use constant-rank nondegeneracy to justify smoothness and the direct sum.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Symplectic neighborhood theorem
items.statement: Assuming AC_ω, symplectomorphic closed embedded symplectic submanifolds with isomorphic symplectic normal bundles have symplectomorphic neighbourhoods inducing the given normal-bundle map.
items.proof_plan: Rerun the tubular proof with the prescribed symplectic-normal complement to realize the full first derivative; then correct the forms by relative Moser.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Canonical symplectic model near the zero section of t star l
items.statement: The canonical model near a Lagrangian L is a neighborhood of the zero section in (T*L,-dλ).
items.proof_plan: Record the zero section and library sign.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Weinstein lagrangian neighborhood theorem
items.statement: A Lagrangian embedding has a neighborhood symplectomorphic to a neighborhood of the zero section in T*L, fixed on L.
items.proof_plan: Identify the normal quotient with T*L by ω-pairing and apply the symplectic-neighborhood theorem.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: Lemma 5.13 and Theorem 5.14 with proof, pp. 62--63

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Lagrangian neighborhood germ is not uniquely determined
items.statement: For the zero section of T*R, the data of a Weinstein Lagrangian neighborhood do not uniquely determine a symplectomorphism germ fixing the section: both the identity and an explicit shear qualify.
items.proof_plan: Compare the identity with the explicit nonidentity shear (q,p)↦(q+p,p), which fixes the zero section and preserves dq∧dp; the proof is choice-free and makes only a nonuniqueness claim.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Characteristic distribution of a coisotropic submanifold is involutive
items.statement: For coisotropic C, ker(ω|TC)=(TC)^ω is a smooth involutive distribution.
items.proof_plan: Constant rank is linear algebra; dω=0 evaluated on two characteristic fields and a tangent field puts their bracket back in the kernel.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: Lecture 9, coisotropic embeddings and characteristic distribution, pp. 52--53

items.title: Local normal form near a coisotropic submanifold
items.statement: Assuming AC_ω, coisotropic presymplectic and characteristic data determine the local symplectic neighborhood germ.
items.proof_plan: Integrate the characteristic bundle by Frobenius, build the conormal/quotient model, match forms on C, and apply relative Moser. No missing foliation premise is implicit.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: Definition 5.16, Theorem 5.18 and special case (a), pp. 63--65

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Every nondegenerate two form is symplectic
items.statement: Every nondegenerate two-form is symplectic.
items.proof_plan: Refute by a nonclosed nondegenerate form in dimension four.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: Lecture 1, definition of a symplectic form, pp. 4--5

items.title: Symplectic manifolds can have odd dimension
items.statement: A symplectic manifold can have odd dimension.
items.proof_plan: Refute tangent-spacewise by even dimensionality.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Every half dimensional submanifold is lagrangian
items.statement: Every half-dimensional submanifold is Lagrangian.
items.proof_plan: Refute with a half-dimensional tangent plane on which ω restricts nontrivially.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: The canonical cotangent symplectic form is d lambda under the library convention
items.statement: The canonical cotangent form is dλ under the library convention.
items.proof_plan: Refute from the declared convention ω_can=-dλ.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Cohomologous symplectic forms on a noncompact manifold are always isotopic
items.statement: Cohomologous symplectic forms on a noncompact manifold are always isotopic.
items.proof_plan: Refute the inference: a symplectic path and global flow control are additional hypotheses.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: Lecture 7, compactness discussion after Theorem 7.3, p. 45

items.title: Darboux theorem makes all symplectic manifolds globally symplectomorphic
items.statement: Darboux makes all equidimensional symplectic manifolds globally symplectomorphic.
items.proof_plan: Refute by topology or symplectic cohomology; Darboux is local.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: Lecture 8, Theorem 8.1 and its local consequence, p. 47

items.proof_plan: Compute its matrix and top wedge.

items.title: Isotropic coisotropic and lagrangian coordinate subspaces
items.statement: Standard coordinate subspaces realize all four symplectic subspace types.

items.proof_plan: Check angular-chart transitions.

items.title: Graphs of exact and closed one forms as lagrangians
items.statement: Graphs of exact and closed one-forms are Lagrangian.
items.proof_plan: Pull back λ; retain the closed/nonexact distinction.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.statement: The diagonal is Lagrangian in M^-×M.

items.title: A compatible complex structure on standard symplectic space
items.statement: J(q,p)=(-p,q) is compatible with the standard form.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Moser isotopy for area forms on a compact surface
items.statement: Equal-total-area positive forms on a compact connected oriented surface are isotopic.
items.proof_plan: Use the top-degree integration criterion, positive interpolation, and Moser.

items.title: Darboux coordinates for a nonconstant area form
items.statement: A positive form f(x,y)dx∧dy has explicit local Darboux coordinates.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: The zero section and cotangent fibres as lagrangians
items.statement: The zero section and cotangent fibres are Lagrangian.
items.proof_plan: Restrict λ or dq and use half dimension.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: A nondegenerate nonclosed two form in dimension at least four
items.statement: On R⁴, dx₁∧dy₁+e^{x₁}dx₂∧dy₂ is nondegenerate but not closed.
items.proof_plan: Compute its square and dω=e^{x₁}dx₁∧dx₂∧dy₂.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Cohomology class obstructs a global symplectomorphism
items.statement: Incompatible symplectic cohomology classes obstruct a global symplectomorphism.
items.proof_plan: Use pullback naturality and integration on a compact example.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: A compatible almost complex structure that is not integrable
items.statement: Compatible almost-complex structures need not be integrable in dimension at least four.
items.proof_plan: Vary the standard compatible structure by a point-dependent symplectic conjugation and compute a nonzero Nijenhuis component.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: Nijenhuis tensor and compatible almost-complex structures, pp. 41--43

items.title: Hamiltonian vector fields are symplectic and symplectic fields are locally hamiltonian

items.title: Hamiltonians for a fixed vector field differ by a locally constant function

items.title: Hamiltonian flows preserve the symplectic form
items.statement: Hamiltonian local flows preserve ω.

items.title: A hamiltonian is conserved along its own flow

items.title: Poisson bracket on a symplectic manifold

items.proof_plan: Record every sign-equivalent formula.

items.title: Poisson bracket is bilinear skew and a derivation in each entry
items.statement: The Poisson bracket is bilinear, skew, and a derivation in each entry.

items.title: Hamiltonian vector field map is a lie antihomomorphism
items.statement: With the library convention, [X_F,X_G]=-X_{ {F,G} }.

items.title: Smooth functions form a poisson algebra
items.statement: C∞(M) is a Poisson algebra.

items.title: Regular common level sets are lagrangian submanifolds
items.statement: For a completely integrable system F=(F_1,...,F_n) on a 2n-manifold, every nonempty regular common level F^{-1}(c) is an n-dimensional Lagrangian submanifold, and at each point its tangent space is spanned by X_F1,...,X_Fn.
items.proof_plan: Apply the regular-level theorem and tangent-kernel proposition to F. Poisson commutation makes every X_Fi tangent and mutually ω-orthogonal; nondegeneracy of ω transfers independence of dF_i to independence of X_Fi, so these n fields span the n-dimensional tangent space and make it Lagrangian.

items.title: Stabilizer of the r n action on a compact connected regular fibre is a full lattice

items.proof_plan: Independent fields make orbits open; connectedness gives one orbit, local freeness gives discreteness, and compactness of R^n/Γ forces full rank.

items.title: Liouville arnold action angle theorem
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. Near a compact connected regular fibre, with a proper submersion and connected nearby fibres, there are action–angle coordinates; every fibre-constant Hamiltonian depends only on I. AC_omega is used through both compact-flow suppliers and directly to select the counterexample sequence in the local period-lattice argument.
items.proof_plan: Use a transverse slice to obtain the fibration, smoothly normalize the period lattice to a torus action, choose a local Lagrangian section, integrate the resulting closed base one-forms for actions, and use the torus action for angles. Remove base–base terms by the Lagrangian section. This is local and does not cover arbitrary Hamiltonians.

items.title: Spherical pendulum monodromy obstructs global action angle coordinates
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. The spherical pendulum regular torus fibration has nontrivial monodromy around its focus-focus value.
items.proof_plan: For F=(H,J) on T*S^2, H=|p|^2/2+z and J=x p_y-y p_x, use Martynchuk–Broer–Efstathiou §3.1 (arXiv PDF pp.7–11) rather than attributing a matrix to Meinrenken. The rotation generated by J fixes the orbit cycle b. Across the unique focus-focus critical value h=1, their proved Takens index theorem gives c(1+epsilon)-c(1-epsilon)=1. Their solid-torus gluing calculation gives M_gamma=T(c_1)T(c_2)^{-1}=T(1), T(c)=[[1,c],[0,1]], in the basis (a,b); reversing loop or basis changes the sign/conjugacy, not nontriviality. Explain the critical-value loop and the Chern-jump/gluing route, then apply the period-lattice obstruction proposition. This advanced example imports the source's Takens theorem and gluing argument explicitly; do not imply those are proved by Meinrenken or by the local Liouville–Arnold theorem.
